title: Advantages and Limitations of Java
subtopics: Situations where other technologies may be more appropriate
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of advantages and limitations of java and identify when it is appropriate in a Java program.
Apply at least one of the lesson topics—portability and backward compatibility—in a small, readable example.
Predict the example result and check it against the stated output or a boundary-case test.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will study advantages and limitations of java with a short explanation, an original visual map, a Java example, and a check you can perform yourself. Focus on the relationship between the rule and the behavior rather than memorizing isolated syntax.
content.why_it_matters: This concept matters because it helps you recognize the Java language, the JVM, and the JDK as related but distinct parts of a development platform. In this lesson, focus on portability and backward compatibility and use a minimal example to check what the rule actually guarantees.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Java source is compiled to class-file bytecode that a compatible JVM can execute. Native libraries, file paths, runtime versions, and platform assumptions can still affect portability. The important habit is to make the assumptions explicit and use the code example as a small experiment.

content_blocks.title: How the pieces fit
content_blocks.text: Connect portability and backward compatibility with memory management before choosing an implementation. The example is a small, observable case; extend it by changing one input and checking a boundary, invalid value, or compatibility limit where relevant.

items.title: Portability and backward compatibility
items.text: Java source is compiled to class-file bytecode that a compatible JVM can execute. Native libraries, file paths, runtime versions, and platform assumptions can still affect portability.

items.title: Memory management
items.text: Java is a general-purpose, statically typed language and a platform. Source code is compiled into class-file bytecode that a compatible JVM can execute; distinguish the language, JVM, JDK tools, and standard APIs. Apply that reasoning specifically to memory management and confirm the result with the example or a targeted test.

items.title: Performance considerations
items.text: Use Path and Files for modern file operations, choose byte or character APIs based on the data, and close resources reliably. Parse external files defensively because their contents may be incomplete or malformed.

items.title: Runtime and memory overhead
items.text: Use the standard library type that matches the data: java.time for dates and zones, BigDecimal for exact decimal arithmetic, and locale-aware APIs for user-facing text and numbers.

content_blocks.run_instructions: Print a small fact about the Java platform. For ordinary Java SE examples, use JDK 25, save a complete class as Main.java, and run `javac Main.java` followed by `java Main`. CodeLeaf does not execute Java in the browser; use a local JDK for these examples. Preview-only and configuration-file examples have their own version or filename notes.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the original example, remove any temporary output files it created, and rerun the baseline case. Do not leave credentials, generated private data, or large test files in the project directory.

content_blocks.title: Professional habit
content_blocks.text: Keep one clear hypothesis per experiment. Check the version, read the error message, test boundaries, and record what evidence supports your conclusion.

content.task: Try it yourself: build the smallest program that demonstrates portability and backward compatibility. Change one input, predict the result, and add one boundary or invalid case before considering the task complete.

common_mistakes.problem: Applying the rule from memory without checking its exact contract.
common_mistakes.why: Small differences in type, scope, API version, or input shape can change the result.
common_mistakes.fix: Inspect the relevant official API/language documentation and build a minimal reproducer.

common_mistakes.problem: Testing only a single happy path.
common_mistakes.why: Boundary values and failures often reveal assumptions hidden by the simplest example.
common_mistakes.fix: Add an empty, boundary, or invalid case and state the expected behavior before running it.

common_mistakes.why: It becomes difficult to identify the actual cause of a different result.
common_mistakes.fix: Change one factor at a time and keep a short record of observed behavior.
